review.title: A/V continuity diagnostics
review.acceptance: Browser playback diagnostics detect and report deterministic A/V continuity proxies with their evidence source and reason trail, never label a proxy as measured A/V skew, never expose a millisecond sync-offset claim without an external measurement source, and document the external flash-and-blip procedure for true A/V offset measurement

performance.evidence: MEASURED on e24d51f, not asserted. The repository has no bench script for apps/web, so a harness was written as a scratch vitest file inside apps/web/src/components/player/diagnostics, typechecked with npx tsc --noEmit before running (it caught nothing on the final version but DID NOT catch the first: the harness had built BufferedRange as {start,end} instead of {startSeconds,endSeconds}, which vitest surfaced as a TypeError inside describeRanges -- reported here because the rule in this project is that a harness defect is reported, not quietly fixed), run with NODE_OPTIONS=--expose-gc, and DELETED before commit. It is not in the tree. Five assertions, all passed, exit 0, 2.60s. CONTROL FIRST, because a timing harness with no control measures nothing: a 400-iteration sqrt loop had to cost more than 5x the cheap call. It measured 0.000739ms vs 0.000124ms, so the timer resolves differences of the size being reported. RESULTS. (1) readVideoFrameMetadata -- the function index.ts names as the one that BELONGS in requestVideoFrameCallback -- costs 0.109 microseconds per call over 500,000 steady-state iterations after a 2,000-call warmup: 0.0007% of a 60 Hz frame budget, against a declared ceiling of 1%. (2) observeAvContinuity composed with summariseAvContinuity costs 4.113 microseconds per call over 100,000 iterations, against a declared ceiling of 1ms for a telemetry tick. (3) The composed report costs 48.3x the per-frame reader. STATED PRECISELY: that ratio CORROBORATES index.ts's 'this is not a per-frame function' warning but does not by itself prove the stronger claim, because 4.113 microseconds is still only 0.025% of a 60 Hz frame in WALL CLOCK -- the header's objection is about ALLOCATION RATE (about a dozen objects per call, so roughly 700 allocations a second at 60 Hz), and allocation rate is not what a wall-clock harness measures. The ratio is the honest form of that evidence and the stronger claim is left to the header's argument. (4) THE NO-HISTORY PROPERTY, which is the one this directory's design actually rests on: 200,000 observations between two forced-gc heapUsed samples moved retained heap by -14,544 bytes -- negative, i.e. inside sampling noise and not growth. Anything genuinely retained per call would be megabytes. That is the measured form of 'nothing here holds history: no growing buffer, no ring, no subscription that outlives a session'. NOT CLAIMED: no browser-side measurement, no real media element, no requestVideoFrameCallback timing on a device. This is Node 22.22.2 on a 2-core container, and it is evidence about the pure functions' cost, which is all this module contains.

review.title: Critical E2E harness
review.acceptance: Catalog to title to player to progress fixture journey is reproducible in CI. MANDATORY ADDITION 2026-09-19, at gpt-architect's round-50 direction when it approved PL-0707, and placed here because THIS TASK OWNS e2e/**: expectedStatus in e2e/src/contract.ts must recognise request_body_too_large as HTTP 413; an E2E case must drive an oversized request and verify 413 PLUS the reason code; and THE E2E HELPER MUST REMAIN INDEPENDENTLY RESTATED rather than importing the server's status function. That last clause is the point of the whole item and must not be optimised away: the helper is a deliberately hand-written mirror, and importing playbackSessionHttpStatus would make the assertion a tautology that passes however wrong the server is. Today the helper derives request-level denials from only request_malformed and request_field_not_permitted, so it would infer 403 where the server correctly answers 413. Nothing fails yet, because no e2e spec sends an oversized body -- the mirror is simply out of date from f83bc65 onward, which is the failure mode a mirror has.

e2e.evidence: EXECUTED, in the CI job's own configuration, on e24d51f. Commands, run from e2e/ with PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH and PLAYWRIGHT_SKIP_BROWSER_DOWNLOAD unset so the PINNED revision resolves from Playwright's default cache, CI=1, and the three variables .github/workflows/ci.yml sets on the e2e job (CONTENT_RIGHTS_ENFORCEMENT=strict, LIBERTY_FC_SEED=20250819, LIBERTY_FIXTURE_MEDIA_ORIGIN=https://fixtures.invalid): (1) LIBERTY_E2E_WEB_MODE=production npm test -- --project=api --project=chromium -> 61 passed, 12 skipped, 0 failed, exit 0; (2) LIBERTY_E2E_WEB_MODE=development npm test -- --project=api --project=chromium -> 70 passed, 3 skipped, 0 failed, exit 0. BOTH MODES, because docs/E2E.md makes the pair the gate: the strings production requires absent are the ones development requires present. Browser: chromium 1234 (Chrome for Testing 151.0.7922.34) from /root/.cache/ms-playwright/chromium-1234, which is the revision e2e/package-lock.json's @playwright/test 1.62.1 pins -- NOT the 1194 substitution the 2026-09-15 evidence was caveated for. retries=0, forbidOnly on. THE REAL JOURNEY RAN: critical-journey.spec.ts executed 10 chromium tests in each mode covering home -> title -> play affordance -> watch route -> player page -> back to catalog, alongside progress.api.spec.ts, catalog.api.spec.ts, search.spec.ts and rights-boundary.api.spec.ts. No unit test, typecheck, build or file-existence claim is offered in place of any of it. THE PL-0707 REQUIREMENT IS IMPLEMENTED AND DRIVEN: three new api-project tests, green in both modes -- 'an oversized body is refused unread, with 413 and a size reason' (asserts status 413, outcome denied, request_body_too_large as the PRIMARY reason, and that the refusal echoes none of the padding), 'a body just under the cap is not refused for its size' (the pairing that stops the first passing against a route that refuses everything), and 'the status mapping this suite checks against is not the server's own' (reads src/contract.ts and fails if any module specifier reaches @liberty, apps/web or the session contract, or if playbackSessionHttpStatus is ever called). NON-VACUITY PROVEN BY MUTATION: replacing the 413 branch with a no-op makes the oversized spec fail 'Expected: 403 / Received: 413' at the decision() status cross-check, exit 1; restored and typechecked clean. SCOPE LIMIT STATED: api and chromium only, exactly the pair the CI job runs. WebKit, mobile-safari and Firefox were NOT launched and this result claims nothing about them; 12 skips in production and 3 in development are the mode-guarded and media-rig-guarded cases. This is a local container run, not a GitHub runner.

recommended.title: A superseded task needs a terminal state that is true
recommended.acceptance: A superseded task has a TRUTHFUL terminal representation, so that a provenance-invalid original whose work shipped under a named successor is neither left BLOCKED forever nor mislabelled as work nobody did. THE GAP, measured rather than asserted. control/policies.json lists eight statuses and exactly two are terminal: DONE and CANCELED. BLOCKED transitions only to BACKLOG, READY or CANCELED. There is NO cancel command on the CLI -- the reachable verbs are validate, sync, status, dispatch, claim, start, gate, review, approve, request-changes, done, block, unblock, release and event -- so CANCELED is currently reachable only by hand-editing control/tasks.json, which is the move the operating contract forbids. And scripts/ai-control-plane.mjs states at its gate-recording guard that CANCELED means 'there is no work to evidence', which is FALSE for a superseded original: the work exists, was reviewed and shipped under the successor's id. THE CONTROL PLANE ALREADY KNOWS ABOUT SUPERSESSION AND DELIBERATELY DOES NOT ACT ON IT. The comment at the supersession detector says a corrective re-run supersedes its predecessor and 'the predecessor is left BLOCKED deliberately -- its provenance record is preserved as audit history rather than repaired, on the rule PL-0703 established', and that BLOCKED can never reach DONE so requireAllDependenciesDone gates every dependent forever. It reports and never repairs, by design. This task does not change that: it adds a way to SAY the thing the detector already notices. REQUIRED: a terminal status that means superseded and says so -- the implementer chooses the spelling and justifies it -- carrying a REQUIRED reference to the successor task id, validated to exist and to be DONE. A status that permits a null successor is not acceptable: the whole content of the claim is which task carries the work now. REQUIRED: a control-plane command to reach it, because a terminal state reachable only by hand-editing the source of truth is worse than no terminal state. The transition must be refused when the named successor is not DONE, and the audit event must carry both ids. REQUIRED: a superseded task must NOT count as DONE in progress figures and must NOT satisfy requireAllDependenciesDone by pretending to be complete. Whether it should satisfy a dependency AT ALL is the design question and the implementer must answer it explicitly: a dependent of a superseded task is almost certainly meant to depend on the successor, and the existing detector already reports exactly that -- so the safe answer may be that supersession does NOT satisfy the dependency and the detector's advice to repoint stands. REQUIRED: the four current instances are the acceptance test, and their subsumption was audited in round 73 before this task was filed. PL-0205 superseded by PL-0207 (DONE), PL-0401 by PL-0405 (DONE), PL-0601 by PL-0603 (DONE), PL-0703 by PL-0706 (DONE). In every case the successor's acceptance was read in full against the original's and found to be a strict superset, not merely a DONE task with a similar name. NOT IN SCOPE: repairing the four originals' provenance, which the reviewer has ruled cannot be done in place; automatically repointing dependencies, which the existing comment refuses on the ground that a self-modifying graph is a larger failure than the one it fixes; and any change that lets a superseded task reach DONE.
recommended.notes: Filed 2026-09-22 from the round-73 subsumption audit gpt-architect ordered at b034460. The reviewer's instruction was explicit: verify subsumption mechanically, preserve the originals' audit history, use a legitimate terminal transition ONLY if one exists and accurately describes the relationship, and -- if the control plane has no truthful terminal representation -- LEAVE THE TASKS BLOCKED AND IMPROVE THE MECHANISM RATHER THAN FALSIFYING HISTORY. The audit found subsumption in all four cases and found no truthful terminal state, so all four stay BLOCKED and this task is the second half of that instruction. The decisive evidence is the control plane's own words: CANCELED is documented in scripts/ai-control-plane.mjs as meaning 'there is no work to evidence', and for these four the work exists and was reviewed. control/tasks.json is in reviewDependencies rather than allowedPaths deliberately: this task builds the mechanism and does not transition the four originals, which is a separate decision for the reviewer once a truthful state exists.
